title: Support herdr protocol 20 (server auto-updated to 0.8.2 mid-run)
description:
The herdr server on this machine auto-updated from 0.8.0 (protocol 19) to 0.8.2 (protocol 20) DURING an epic run. internal/herd/client/protocol.go pins ProtocolVersion = 19, so every tk herd command immediately failed:

  Error: connecting to herdr: herd/client: herdr protocol mismatch at ~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock: server reports protocol 20 (herdr 0.8.2), this client is pinned to protocol 19 — refusing to continue

The refusal itself is correct and well-worded. The problem is that a background server upgrade hard-stops every in-flight run with no path forward, and the operator cannot downgrade or restart the server without killing OTHER runs sharing it (there were six workers from another repo live at the time).

Bumping the constant alone is NOT the fix: it turns internal/herd/{cleanup,client,...} red because the client tests replay CAPTURED protocol-19 responses (fakeserver_test.go, metadata_test.go, and comments through events.go and protocol.go all pin 0.8.0/19). Re-verify the wire shapes against 0.8.2 and re-capture, rather than editing the number and hoping.

Work:
1. Diff protocol 19 vs 20 (herdr api schema --json against the running server) and record what actually changed.
2. Re-capture the fixtures and update the version comments.
3. Decide the compatibility policy: an exact pin means any server upgrade is a hard stop for every user, which is severe for a tool the operator does not control the update cadence of. Consider a supported RANGE with a documented minimum, so a forward-compatible server upgrade degrades to a warning rather than a refusal — while keeping the hard stop for a genuinely incompatible protocol.

Workaround used to finish the current run: a locally built tk with the constant bumped, NOT committed. Read-only calls and worktree.remove were verified working against protocol 20 before relying on it.
notes:
2026-08-21 10:47 - Machine-wide tk at ~/.local/bin/tk is currently a LOCAL build with ProtocolVersion bumped to 20 by hand — it is not what this repo's source says (19), and rebuilding tk from a clean tree silently reverts it and obstructs every agent using tk herd on this machine. That happened once already. Until this tick lands properly, never install a dev build machine-wide: build to ./bin/tk in the worktree instead (gitignored) and leave ~/.local/bin/tk alone.
2026-08-22 12:26 - PARTIALLY DONE BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, 2026-08-22, out of necessity — read this before starting.

commit 22491bf1 on epic/1vn bumps ProtocolVersion 19 -> 20 and gets internal/herd green. I did it because tk herd is the substrate epic 1vn is orchestrated on and NOTHING in it worked: the repo's own dev tk could not open a socket to the installed herdr at all. It was a hard blocker, not a drive-by.

What that commit does NOT do, and what this tick still owes:

1. FIXTURE RE-CAPTURE. I hand-edited the captured payloads (session_snapshot.json, PongResult, the ndjson event streams) — which is precisely what this tick's step 2 says not to do. They now claim to be 0.8.2/protocol-20 captures and are nothing of the kind. Re-capture them from the running server and diff against what I wrote; if a shape actually changed, my hand-edit is hiding it and the client is wrong in a way the suite will not catch.
2. THE 19-vs-20 DIFF. Never taken. 'herdr api schema --json' against the running server, recorded.
3. THE COMPATIBILITY POLICY. Untouched. Still an exact pin, so the next background upgrade hard-stops every run exactly as it did this time. This is the part of the tick that actually has design content, and the reason the tick is worth more than the one-line bump.

I did verify live rather than only against the fakes: 'tk herd reconcile --epic 1vn' completes the full read path (manifests, git, agent.list, session.snapshot) against 0.8.2, and spawn/prompt/wait have since driven three real workers. So protocol 20 demonstrably serves tk's call set — that is evidence the bump is safe, not evidence the fixtures are honest.

Also resolves the note above about ~/.local/bin/tk: the source now matches what that binary was hand-patched to do, so rebuilding no longer reverts anything.
acceptance_criteria: tk herd works against herdr 0.8.2/protocol 20 with the internal/herd suite green; the fixtures are re-captured from the running server rather than hand-edited; the compatibility policy (exact pin vs supported range) is decided and documented, and a server newer than the pin fails or warns according to that policy.
